Short Description: FDA-approved neuromodulator to smooth fine lines, forehead creases & crow’s feet.
Full Description: Botox (Botulinum toxin type A) is a purified protein injection that temporarily relaxes facial muscles causing dynamic wrinkles. It is the gold standard worldwide for softening forehead lines, frown lines between the eyebrows (glabella), and crow’s feet around the eyes, leaving your expression refreshed and naturally rested.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Horizontal forehead lines & furrows
2. Frown lines between eyebrows (11 lines)
3. Crow’s feet around the eyes
4. Bunny lines on the nose
5. Jawline slimming & masseter reduction
6. Excessive underarm sweating (Hyperhidrosis)
Key Benefits:
• Visible wrinkle reduction in 4 to 7 days
• Quick 15–20 minute in-clinic procedure
• Zero downtime — return to work immediately
• Preserves natural facial expressions when administered by experts
• Prevents deeper wrinkle formation over time
What To Expect: Your dermatologist will assess facial muscle dynamics and mark injection points. Tiny micro-injections are delivered using ultra-fine needles. You will feel a minor pinch lasting only a few seconds. Mild redness or tiny bumps resolve within 30 minutes.
Sessions & Frequency: Single session delivers results lasting 3 to 5 months. Maintenance sessions are recommended 2–3 times a year.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime. Avoid touching the area, strenuous workouts, and lying down flat for 4 hours post-procedure.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Mild temporary redness or pinprick bruising
• Avoid blood-thinning supplements 48 hours prior
• Not recommended during pregnancy or breastfeeding
• Always performed by certified MD Dermatologists for optimal symmetry
FAQs:
Q: Will my face look frozen or unnatural?
A: No. When administered by our verified board-certified dermatologists, precise micro-dosing softens lines while maintaining natural, expressive facial movement.

Q: How long does Botox take to show full results?
A: Initial effects appear in 3–5 days, with peak, optimal smoothing visible at 10–14 days.

Q: How many units will I need?
A: Units depend on your muscle strength and target zones (typically 12–20 units for forehead, 16–24 for crow’s feet). Your doctor will customize this during consultation.

Short Description: Hyaluronic acid gels to restore lost facial volume, plump lips and sculpt contours.
Full Description: Dermal fillers are formulated with biocompatible Hyaluronic Acid (HA) to instantly restore facial volume, lift sagging cheeks, define the jawline, soften smile lines (nasolabial folds), and hydrate lips.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Lip definition, plumping and hydration
2. Cheekbone contouring & volume restoration
3. Under-eye hollows & tear trough brightening
4. Jawline sculpting & chin enhancement
5. Smile lines (Nasolabial folds) softening
Key Benefits:
• Instant, visible lifting and volume
• High safety profile with dissolvable Hyaluronic Acid
• Natural-looking enhancement tailored to your bone structure
• Long-lasting results from 9 to 18 months
What To Expect: Numbing cream is applied for 20 minutes. Fillers containing built-in lidocaine are carefully placed using fine micro-cannulas or needles for maximum precision and minimal bruising.
Sessions & Frequency: Single session delivers immediate results. Touch-ups are typically scheduled once every 12 months.
Downtime & Recovery: 1 to 2 days of mild swelling or localized tenderness. Normal activities can resume immediately.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Mild swelling is normal for the first 24–48 hours
• Avoid excessive heat, saunas, and intense workouts for 48 hours
• Choose verified injectors with deep anatomical expertise
FAQs:
Q: Are dermal fillers reversible?
A: Yes. Hyaluronic acid fillers can be instantly dissolved using an enzyme called Hyaluronidase if adjustment is ever desired.

Q: How soon can I see results?
A: Results are noticeable immediately, with optimal settling occurring within 7 to 10 days after mild swelling subsides.

Short Description: Medical-grade 3-in-1 hydradermabrasion: cleanse, extract blackheads & infuse antioxidant serums.
Full Description: Hydrafacial MD is a patented medical-grade skin treatment that uses Vortex-Fusion technology to deeply cleanse pores, extract sebum and blackheads painlessly, and saturate the skin with intensive hydration, peptides, and botanical antioxidants.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Clogged pores, blackheads and whiteheads
2. Dull, tired or dehydrated skin
3. Uneven skin texture and tone
4. Pre-event instant luminous glow
Key Benefits:
• Instant radiant glow with zero redness or peeling
• Deeply cleanses congested pores without manual squeezing
• Customizable booster serums for anti-ageing or brightening
• Safe for all skin types and skin tones year-round
What To Expect: A gentle, soothing 45-minute treatment across 3 steps: Cleansing & Exfoliation, Acid Peel & Vortex Extraction, followed by Antioxidant & Hyaluronic Acid Infusion.
Sessions & Frequency: Recommended once a month for optimal skin health, or 2–3 days before special occasions.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime. You can wear makeup immediately, although you will love your natural bare glow.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Gentle on sensitive skin
• Avoid active retinol/AHA acids 24 hours prior
FAQs:
Q: Is Hydrafacial painful?
A: Not at all. Most patients describe it as a cool paintbrush moving across the face, followed by a gentle suction sensation.

Q: Can I do Hydrafacial before a wedding or party?
A: Yes! It is the ideal red-carpet glow treatment. We recommend getting it done 24–48 hours before your event.

Short Description: Dermatologist-formulated peeling solutions for acne, active breakouts, stubborn tan & dark spots.
Full Description: A clinical chemical peel uses controlled organic exfoliating acids (Glycolic, Salicylic, Lactic, Mandelic, or TCA) to safely dissolve the outer layer of dead, sun-damaged skin cells, accelerating cellular turnover to reveal smoother, even-toned skin.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Active acne breakouts and post-acne pigmentation
2. Sun tan, uneven pigmentation and melasma
3. Enlarged pores and rough texture
4. Superficial fine lines and dullness
Key Benefits:
• Rapid clearance of active breakouts and blackheads
• Fades dark acne marks (PIH) and sun spots
• Refines pore size and restores smooth texture
• Tailored peel strength customized to Indian skin types
What To Expect: The skin is thoroughly degreased before applying the selected chemical peel solution. You will experience a mild warm or tingling sensation for 3 to 7 minutes before neutralizer is applied.
Sessions & Frequency: Series of 4 to 6 sessions spaced 2 to 3 weeks apart for best transformative results.
Downtime & Recovery: Mild flaking or micro-peeling for 2 to 4 days depending on peel depth. Strict sun protection is required.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Sunscreen application (SPF 50+) is mandatory post-peel
• Do not pick or scratch flaking skin
• Discontinue retinoids 3 days before treatment
FAQs:
Q: Will my whole face peel visibly in sheets?
A: Modern superficial and medium peels produce gentle micro-flaking rather than dramatic sheet peeling, allowing you to carry on with your daily routine.

Short Description: Precision collagen induction therapy to diminish acne scars, shrink pores & firm skin.
Full Description: Microneedling (Collagen Induction Therapy) uses an automated medical device with microscopic sterile needles to create controlled micro-channels in the dermis. This triggers the skin’s natural healing cascade, boosting collagen and elastin production.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Depressed acne scars (boxcar, rolling, icepick)
2. Enlarged open pores and uneven texture
3. Fine lines and loss of skin elasticity
4. Surgical scars and stretch marks
Key Benefits:
• Significant improvement in acne scar depth and texture
• Stimulates body’s own natural collagen production
• Enhances topical serum absorption by over 300%
• Safe for darker skin tones with minimal risk of pigmentation
What To Expect: Topical numbing cream is applied for 30–45 minutes for a comfortable experience. The Dermapen device is gently passed across the target zones with calming hyaluronic acid or growth factor serums.
Sessions & Frequency: 3 to 5 sessions spaced 4 weeks apart deliver permanent collagen remodeling benefits.
Downtime & Recovery: 1 to 2 days of mild sunburn-like redness. Mineral makeup can be applied after 24 hours.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Avoid direct sun exposure for 48 hours
• Keep skin hydrated with dermatologist-recommended barrier creams
FAQs:
Q: Does microneedling hurt?
A: With our clinical-grade topical numbing cream, discomfort is very low — most patients feel only a slight vibration or light scratch.

Short Description: US-FDA approved Triple-Wavelength Diode & Alexandrite lasers for painless, permanent hair reduction.
Full Description: Laser Hair Removal uses concentrated laser light beams absorbed by the melanin in hair follicles. The thermal energy destroys the follicle root, permanently stunting future hair growth while keeping surrounding skin cool and protected with advanced contact cooling tips.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Full body hair reduction (legs, arms, back, chest)
2. Facial hair (upper lip, chin, jawline, sideburns)
3. Bikini line and underarms
4. Ingrown hair and strawberry legs prevention
Key Benefits:
• Up to 90% permanent hair reduction
• Completely eliminates painful waxing, razor bumps & ingrown hairs
• Advanced ice-cooling handpieces ensure virtually painless sessions
• Safe and effective on all Indian skin types
What To Expect: The area is shaved and marked. A cooling gel is applied, and the laser handpiece glides smoothly across the skin delivering rapid pulses with ice-cold contact cooling.
Sessions & Frequency: 6 to 8 sessions spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart, matching the active hair growth cycles (anagen phase).
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime. Mild transient redness usually resolves within 1 to 2 hours.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Shave target area 24 hours prior; avoid waxing or plucking for 3 weeks
• Avoid tanning or active sun exposure before sessions
FAQs:
Q: Is Laser Hair Removal permanent?
A: It provides long-term permanent hair reduction (80–90% reduction). Any remaining fine hairs grow back much slower, lighter, and softer, requiring only an occasional yearly maintenance session.

Short Description: Nanosecond Nd:YAG laser to fragment deep melanin, clarify skin tone & stimulate collagen.
Full Description: Q-Switched Nd:YAG laser toning delivers safe, non-ablative high-energy nanosecond pulses that shatter stubborn deep pigmentation and dermal melanin deposits into microscopic fragments, which your body naturally clears over subsequent weeks.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Stubborn melasma and hyperpigmentation
2. Sun damage, dark patches and age spots
3. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH)
4. Dull skin tone and overall carbon laser peel glow
Key Benefits:
• Targets deep dermal pigmentation without burning the surface skin
• Evens out patchy skin tone and brightens complexion
• Stimulates deep collagen renewal to shrink pores
• No peeling or visible skin breakage
What To Expect: You will wear protective eye goggles. The laser pulses feel like tiny warm rubber band snaps across the face. The session takes about 20 minutes.
Sessions & Frequency: 4 to 6 sessions every 2–3 weeks for progressive, lasting skin clarity.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime. Mild warmth or pinkness subsides within 30 minutes.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen is essential to maintain results
FAQs:
Q: Can Q-Switched laser worsen pigmentation?
A: When performed by skilled dermatologists using certified machines with proper cooling protocols, Q-Switched toning is exceptionally safe for Asian skin types.

Short Description: Multi-modality scar remodeling: Subcision, TCA Cross, Fractional CO2 / Erbium Laser & MNRF.
Full Description: Comprehensive acne scar revision tailored to your scar types (icepick, boxcar, and rolling scars). Combines subcision to release tethered fibrous bands with Fractional Resurfacing and Microneedle Radiofrequency (MNRF) for profound collagen rebuilding.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Rolling scars and tethered depressions
2. Boxcar scars and uneven dermal indentations
3. Deep icepick scars (treated with TCA Cross)
4. Enlarged textural pores and rough scar margins
Key Benefits:
• Clinically proven 60–80% improvement in scar depth
• Multi-modality customized approach based on scar mapping
• Permanent scar restructuring and collagen elevation
What To Expect: Detailed scar mapping under tangential lighting, followed by local numbing. Subcision releases bound scar tissue, followed by fractional laser or MNRF energy passes.
Sessions & Frequency: 3 to 5 combination sessions spaced 4 to 6 weeks apart.
Downtime & Recovery: 3 to 5 days of micro-crusting and mild redness. Skin settles smoothly with diligent moisturizer use.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Active acne should be controlled before scar revision
• Avoid sun exposure during the healing window
FAQs:
Q: Are acne scar treatment results permanent?
A: Yes! The new collagen synthesized during the healing cascade permanently elevates and smoothens the depressed scar tissue.

Short Description: Targeted protocols combining medical depigmentation peels, laser toning & tyrosinase inhibitors.
Full Description: A multi-layered dermatological protocol designed to regulate excess melanin production at the cellular level. Combines Cosmelan / Dermamelan peels, Nd:YAG laser toning, and clinical antioxidant mesotherapy to lighten stubborn dark patches and melasma.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Hormonal melasma and butterfly patches
2. Sun freckles, age spots and lentigines
3. Dark under-eye circles and peri-oral pigmentation
4. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
Key Benefits:
• Fades deep dermal and epidermal pigmentation
• Suppresses overactive melanocyte activity
• Restores uniform complexion and luminosity
What To Expect: Dermatologist examination using Wood’s lamp or digital dermoscopy to determine pigmentation depth, followed by targeted peel or laser application.
Sessions & Frequency: 3 to 6 sessions customized to the severity and depth of pigmentation.
Downtime & Recovery: Minimal to 2 days of mild peeling depending on the specific protocol used.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Requires consistent homecare regimen and strict sun defense
FAQs:
Q: Can melasma be cured completely?
A: Melasma can be dramatically faded and controlled with clinical treatments and proper maintenance, though sun protection is vital to prevent recurrence.

Short Description: Customized dermatologist medi-facials with Glutathione, Vitamin C infusions & Oxygen therapy.
Full Description: Clinical-grade medi-facials engineered by dermatologists to revitalize fatigued skin. Utilizes ultrasonic sonophoresis, oxygen dome therapy, and active infusions of pure Vitamin C, Glutathione, and Hyaluronic acid for an immediate, healthy glass-skin radiance.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dull, stressed and polluted skin
2. Pre-wedding and festive skin prep
3. Dehydrated skin needing deep moisture infusion
4. Uneven skin tone and environmental damage
Key Benefits:
• Instant glass-skin glow with intense hydration
• Detoxifies and infuses pure botanical antioxidants
• Completely relaxing with zero discomfort
What To Expect: Relaxing multi-step treatment including ultrasonic pore cleanse, antioxidant serum infusion, lymphatic drainage massage, and cooling hydrogel mask.
Sessions & Frequency: Can be done as a single pre-event treatment or monthly for continuous maintenance.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Suitable for all skin types including sensitive skin
FAQs:
Q: How is a Medi-Facial different from a regular salon facial?
A: Medi-facials use pharmaceutical-grade active ingredients, sterile medical equipment, and proven scientific protocols tailored by dermatologists rather than standard cosmetic creams.

Short Description: Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma rich in growth factors to reverse hair thinning & stimulate follicles.
Full Description: Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) therapy utilizes your own blood’s concentrated platelets, rich in bioactive growth factors (PDGF, VEGF, TGF-beta). When injected into thinning areas of the scalp, it awakens dormant hair follicles, strengthens hair roots, and increases hair shaft diameter.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Early to moderate androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss)
2. Diffuse hair thinning and excessive shedding
3. Telogen effluvium (post-stress or illness hair fall)
4. Post-hair transplant graft nourishment
Key Benefits:
• 100% natural, using your body’s own healing platelets
• Clinically proven to reduce hair fall within 2–3 sessions
• Increases hair thickness and overall scalp density
• No risk of allergy or foreign body reaction
What To Expect: A small blood sample (15–20 ml) is drawn and spun in a specialized centrifuge to isolate the golden platelet-rich layer. The scalp is numbed with cooling spray and tiny micro-droplets are delivered into the scalp.
Sessions & Frequency: Initial protocol of 4 sessions spaced 3 to 4 weeks apart, followed by maintenance every 4 to 6 months.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero to few hours of mild scalp tightness. You can wash your hair the following morning.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Stay well hydrated before your appointment
• Avoid anti-inflammatory pain medication 48 hours prior
FAQs:
Q: When will I start seeing hair growth?
A: Reduced hair shedding is typically noticed after 2 sessions. Visible new baby hair growth and thickening of existing strands appear around the 3rd to 4th month.

Short Description: High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound & Radiofrequency to lift jowls, tighten neck & firm skin.
Full Description: Non-surgical skin tightening uses focused ultrasound energy (HIFU) or multi-polar radiofrequency (RF) to heat deep dermal and SMAS layers (the foundation layer tightened in surgical facelifts). This triggers immediate collagen contraction and long-term synthesis.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Mild to moderate jowl sagging and jawline softening
2. Double chin reduction and neck tightening
3. Brow lifting and upper eyelid heaviness
4. Nasolabial fold lifting and cheek elevation
Key Benefits:
• Non-surgical facelift alternative with no incisions or scars
• Lifts and defines the lower face and jawline
• Collagen building continues for up to 6 months post-treatment
• Single-session treatment with results lasting 12–18 months
What To Expect: Ultrasound gel is applied to the target zones. The HIFU transducer delivers focused energy pulses at precise depths (1.5mm, 3.0mm, and 4.5mm). You will feel warm prickling pulses along the jawline and cheekbones.
Sessions & Frequency: Single session is usually sufficient, with annual maintenance.
Downtime & Recovery: Zero downtime. Mild tenderness along the jawline for a few days indicates active collagen remodeling.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Best suited for mild to moderate skin laxity
FAQs:
Q: How does HIFU compare to surgical facelifts?
A: HIFU is non-invasive, requires zero incisions or recovery time, and delivers natural, subtle lifting by stimulating your own collagen, making it ideal for preventative and moderate age-related laxity.

Short Description: Dermatologist-guided facial treatment using clinical cleansing, exfoliation and skin-conditioning steps.
Full Description: A medical facial is a clinician-supervised skin treatment rather than a single standardized procedure. The protocol can combine cleansing, gentle exfoliation, extraction when appropriate, hydration and targeted topical products based on the patient's skin and goals.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dull or tired-looking skin
2. Mild congestion
3. Dry or dehydrated skin
4. Short-term skin refresh before an event
Key Benefits:
• Removes superficial buildup
• Can improve temporary smoothness and hydration
• Protocol can be adapted to the patient's skin
What To Expect: Skin is assessed first. The face is cleansed and the selected exfoliation, extraction, infusion or soothing steps are performed. The final products are chosen to support the skin barrier.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a single treatment; repeat frequency depends on the protocol and skin needs.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually little to no downtime; mild temporary redness can occur after exfoliation or extraction.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Tell the clinician about active skin conditions and current products
• Use gentle skincare and sunscreen after treatment
• Avoid aggressive exfoliation until the skin has recovered
FAQs:
Q: Is a medical facial the same as a salon facial?
A: Not necessarily. A medical facial is performed under clinical supervision and should be selected according to the patient's skin condition and goals.

Short Description: An umbrella term for treatments that improve skin texture, tone, pigmentation, hydration or early signs of ageing.
Full Description: Skin rejuvenation is not one procedure. Depending on the concern, a dermatologist may use chemical peels, microneedling, lasers, radiofrequency or other treatments to improve the appearance and quality of the skin.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Uneven tone or texture
2. Dullness or photodamage
3. Fine lines
4. Early loss of firmness
Key Benefits:
• Can target several visible signs of skin ageing
• Treatment can be tailored to skin type and concern
• Different modalities can be combined when clinically appropriate
What To Expect: The clinician assesses skin type, pigmentation, texture and goals before choosing a modality. Treatment experience and recovery depend on what is selected.
Sessions & Frequency: Varies widely by modality; some treatments are single-session while others are performed as a series.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from none to several days depending on the treatment selected.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• A diagnosis and skin assessment should guide treatment selection
• Darker skin may have greater risk of pigment changes after some laser procedures
• Follow modality-specific aftercare
FAQs:
Q: What is the best skin-rejuvenation treatment?
A: There is no single best option. The appropriate treatment depends on the concern, skin type, desired result and tolerance for downtime.

Short Description: Skin-refresh treatments aimed at improving the appearance of dullness, uneven tone and surface texture.
Full Description: This is a treatment category rather than one standardized procedure. Depending on the patient's skin, a dermatologist may use gentle exfoliation, hydration, medical facial techniques or selected light/laser treatments to improve visible radiance.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dull complexion
2. Mild uneven tone
3. Surface roughness
4. Pre-event skin refresh
Key Benefits:
• Can improve visible brightness and smoothness
• May improve temporary dehydration-related dullness
• Usually requires less recovery than aggressive resurfacing
What To Expect: The skin is assessed and the clinician chooses a low-irritation protocol. Cleansing, exfoliation and hydration are common components, but the exact steps vary.
Sessions & Frequency: Often one treatment for a short-term refresh; maintenance depends on the selected procedure.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually minimal; mild redness or sensitivity can occur depending on exfoliation or device used.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Persistent pigmentation should be assessed rather than treated as simple 'dullness'
• Use sunscreen consistently
• Avoid irritating products immediately after treatment
FAQs:
Q: Does a glow treatment permanently remove pigmentation?
A: No. It may improve the appearance of uneven tone, but persistent pigmentation needs diagnosis and a targeted treatment plan.

Short Description: Treatments designed to improve skin hydration and support the skin barrier.
Full Description: Hydration treatments can use topical products, device-assisted delivery or injectable skin boosters depending on the clinical goal. They are intended to improve the appearance and feel of dehydrated skin rather than permanently change facial structure.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dry or dehydrated skin
2. Tight or rough-feeling skin
3. Dehydration-related fine lines
4. Dull appearance
Key Benefits:
• Improves skin softness and hydration
• Can support the skin barrier
• May reduce the appearance of dehydration lines
What To Expect: The clinician identifies whether the issue is dryness, dehydration, barrier damage or another condition. Treatment may involve cleansing, hydrating actives and barrier-supportive products.
Sessions & Frequency: Depends on modality; topical/device-based treatments may be repeated every few weeks, while injectable boosters follow product-specific protocols.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually little to no downtime for non-injectable protocols; injectable boosters can cause temporary redness, swelling or bruising.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Tell the clinician about active dermatitis or infection
• Avoid aggressive actives if the barrier is irritated
• Injectable treatments require medical assessment
FAQs:
Q: How long do hydration results last?
A: Results are generally temporary and depend on the treatment, skin condition and ongoing skincare.

Short Description: Laser-based facial treatment using a carbon lotion followed by laser energy to refresh the skin.
Full Description: A carbon laser peel, often called a carbon facial, uses a carbon-containing lotion on the skin followed by laser passes. It is commonly marketed for oily skin, visible pores and dullness; results and suitability depend on the laser settings and the underlying concern.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Oily or congested skin
2. Dull appearance
3. Visible pores
4. Mild uneven texture
Key Benefits:
• Can temporarily improve surface smoothness and brightness
• May reduce surface oiliness
• Usually has limited recovery
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed, carbon lotion is applied and allowed to settle, then laser passes are performed with protective eyewear. A soothing product is usually applied afterward.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a series, commonly spaced several weeks apart; exact number depends on the indication and response.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually minimal; temporary warmth or redness is possible.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Laser choice and settings should be individualized
• Darker skin can be more prone to post-inflammatory pigment changes after laser treatment
• Strict sun protection is important
FAQs:
Q: Does a carbon laser peel cause the same peeling as a chemical peel?
A: Usually no. It is primarily a laser-based treatment and typically causes much less visible peeling than a medium or deep chemical peel.

Short Description: Low-fluence laser treatment used to target unwanted pigmentation and improve overall skin tone.
Full Description: Laser toning commonly uses low-fluence, short-pulsed Nd:YAG laser energy to target pigment with relatively low surface injury. It is used in selected cases of pigmentation and uneven tone, but treatment parameters and suitability are important because pigmentary complications can occur.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected facial hyperpigmentation
2. Uneven skin tone
3. Some sun-related pigmentation
4. Selected melasma protocols under specialist care
Key Benefits:
• Can reduce the appearance of selected pigmentation
• Usually has limited downtime when appropriately performed
• Can be used as part of a broader pigmentation plan
What To Expect: Protective eyewear is used and the laser is delivered in multiple passes. The treated skin may feel warm or mildly pink afterward.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually requires multiple sessions spaced weeks apart; the schedule depends on diagnosis and response.
Downtime & Recovery: Often minimal; temporary redness or warmth can occur.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• Pigmentation must be diagnosed before treatment
• Melasma can recur and laser is not always first-line therapy
• Darker skin has increased risk of burns or post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
• Sun protection is essential
FAQs:
Q: Is laser toning suitable for all pigmentation?
A: No. Different causes of pigmentation respond differently, and some conditions can worsen with aggressive laser treatment.

Short Description: Intense pulsed light treatment that targets selected pigment and vascular changes and can improve overall skin appearance.
Full Description: IPL uses a broad spectrum of non-coherent light rather than a single laser wavelength. Depending on the device and settings, it can target superficial brown pigment, redness and some photoaging changes.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Freckles and selected sun spots
2. Facial redness from superficial vessels
3. Uneven skin tone
4. Some photoaging changes
Key Benefits:
• Can improve selected pigment and redness
• Can create more even-looking skin tone
• Non-surgical treatment with relatively short recovery
What To Expect: Protective eyewear is used. Short pulses of light are delivered over the skin; treated pigment may temporarily darken before fading.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a series of treatments several weeks apart; the exact course depends on the indication.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually mild redness and swelling for hours to a few days; pigmented spots may darken temporarily.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions:
• IPL is not suitable for every skin tone or every pigment disorder
• Recent tanning increases risk of burns/pigment changes
• Sun protection before and after treatment is important
FAQs:
Q: Is IPL the same as a laser?
A: No. IPL emits a broad range of light wavelengths, while a laser generally emits a specific wavelength.

Short Description: Alpha-hydroxy-acid peel using glycolic acid to exfoliate the outer skin layers.
Full Description: Glycolic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) used in superficial chemical peels. Concentration, pH and contact time determine depth, so medical protocols should be individualized.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dull complexion
2. Uneven texture
3. Mild acne or post-acne marks
4. Fine superficial lines
Key Benefits:
• Exfoliates superficial skin cells
• Can improve texture and brightness
• May help selected acne and pigment concerns
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed and the acid is applied for a controlled period, then neutralized or removed according to the formulation. Mild stinging is common.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series of superficial peels spaced a few weeks apart; exact protocol varies.
Downtime & Recovery: Mild redness, dryness or flaking for a few days is possible.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid use on actively irritated or infected skin. Sun protection is essential. Stronger peels have greater risk of irritation and pigment change.
FAQs:
Q: Is Glycolic Acid Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Beta-hydroxy-acid peel particularly useful for oily, acne-prone and congested skin.
Full Description: Salicylic acid is a lipophilic beta-hydroxy acid that penetrates into oily follicles and is commonly used in superficial peels for acne and comedonal congestion.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Comedonal acne
2. Oily or congested skin
3. Post-acne marks
4. Rough texture
Key Benefits:
• Helps exfoliate inside and around follicles
• Can reduce comedonal congestion
• May improve superficial post-acne discoloration
What To Expect: The skin is prepared and the peel is applied for a controlled period. Mild tingling or stinging can occur, followed by dryness or light peeling.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a series every few weeks; response and tolerance guide the schedule.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually mild redness and dryness, with light peeling possible.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid on irritated/broken skin. Tell the clinician about aspirin/salicylate sensitivity and all active skincare. Use sunscreen.
FAQs:
Q: Is Salicylic Acid Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Gentle alpha-hydroxy-acid peel used for superficial exfoliation and skin brightening.
Full Description: Lactic acid is an AHA that can exfoliate the stratum corneum while also acting as a humectant. It is commonly used in superficial peel protocols when a milder exfoliating approach is desired.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dull skin
2. Mild uneven tone
3. Rough surface texture
4. Dry-looking skin
Key Benefits:
• Gentle superficial exfoliation
• Can improve smoothness and brightness
• Often chosen when a milder peel is appropriate
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed, the peel is applied and then removed or neutralized according to the product protocol.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series at intervals of a few weeks when clinically indicated.
Downtime & Recovery: Minimal to mild redness, dryness or flaking.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Do not use on compromised skin. Sun protection is important. Avoid combining multiple strong exfoliants without clinician guidance.
FAQs:
Q: Is Lactic Acid Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Superficial AHA peel using mandelic acid for gradual exfoliation and tone/texture improvement.
Full Description: Mandelic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid with a larger molecular structure than glycolic acid, resulting in slower penetration. It is used in superficial peel protocols for texture, acne and uneven pigmentation.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Mild acne and congestion
2. Uneven tone
3. Dullness
4. Rough texture
Key Benefits:
• Provides controlled superficial exfoliation
• Can improve skin smoothness and tone
• Often selected when a gentler peel is preferred
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed and the peel is applied for a controlled time before removal or neutralization. Mild tingling may occur.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually performed as a series of superficial treatments spaced several weeks apart.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually mild redness or dryness; visible peeling may be limited.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Individualize for skin sensitivity and pigment risk. Avoid irritated skin and follow post-peel sun protection.
FAQs:
Q: Is Mandelic Acid Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Trichloroacetic-acid peel whose depth varies with concentration and application technique.
Full Description: TCA can produce superficial to deeper chemical injury depending on concentration and technique. Superficial TCA peels may improve pigmentation and texture; deeper peels carry substantially more risk and should only be performed by appropriately trained clinicians.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected pigmentation
2. Sun-damaged skin
3. Texture irregularity
4. Selected superficial scars
Key Benefits:
• Controlled exfoliation and resurfacing
• Can improve selected pigmentation and texture
• Stronger concentrations reach deeper skin layers
What To Expect: The clinician prepares the skin and applies TCA in a controlled manner. Frosting, burning or stinging can occur depending on depth. Aftercare is important while the skin heals.
Sessions & Frequency: Superficial protocols may be repeated after several weeks; deeper peels are less frequent and require longer recovery.
Downtime & Recovery: Superficial peels may flake for several days; deeper peels can require substantially longer healing.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • TCA depth must be carefully controlled. There is risk of burns, infection and post-inflammatory pigment changes, particularly in darker skin. Strict aftercare is essential.
FAQs:
Q: Is TCA Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Multi-acid superficial peel selected to address acne, congestion and post-acne discoloration.
Full Description: Combination peels use more than one exfoliating ingredient, commonly selected according to acne severity, oiliness and pigmentation. The formulation and strength vary by product and clinician.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Acne and comedones
2. Post-acne marks
3. Oily skin
4. Uneven texture
Key Benefits:
• Can reduce superficial congestion
• May improve post-acne discoloration
• Can smooth surface texture
What To Expect: After cleansing and preparation, the selected peel is applied for a controlled time and removed or neutralized according to the formulation.
Sessions & Frequency: Typically performed as a series several weeks apart when appropriate.
Downtime & Recovery: Mild redness, dryness and peeling are common with superficial protocols.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Active dermatitis, infection or significant irritation may require postponement. Avoid unapproved at-home combinations and use sunscreen.
FAQs:
Q: Is Combination / Acne Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Chemical peel protocol selected to reduce the appearance of excess superficial pigment.
Full Description: Pigmentation peels may use agents such as glycolic acid, salicylic acid, lactic acid or TCA, depending on the diagnosis. A peel should follow assessment of the cause of pigmentation rather than treating every dark patch the same way.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected superficial hyperpigmentation
2. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
3. Some sun-related pigmentation
4. Selected melasma protocols
Key Benefits:
• Can reduce superficial excess pigment
• May improve uneven tone
• Often combined with sun protection and topical therapy
What To Expect: The clinician identifies the type and depth of pigmentation, then applies a selected peel under controlled conditions.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series of treatments spaced weeks apart; maintenance may be required for recurrent pigmentation.
Downtime & Recovery: Mild to moderate peeling depending on depth.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Pigmentation can worsen after inflammation, especially in darker skin. Diagnosis and strict photoprotection are important.
FAQs:
Q: Is Pigmentation Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: A carefully selected superficial peel protocol for pigmentation or texture around the eyes.
Full Description: Periocular skin is thin and sensitive. Under-eye peels, when used, require conservative formulations and careful placement by an experienced clinician; they are not appropriate for every cause of dark circles.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected periocular pigmentation
2. Mild surface texture changes
3. Selected superficial discoloration
Key Benefits:
• May improve selected superficial pigmentation
• Can smooth surface texture
• Non-surgical option when an appropriate cause is identified
What To Expect: The area is assessed carefully and a conservative peel may be applied with strict avoidance of the eye surface. Burning or irritation should not be ignored.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series if indicated, with intervals determined by the clinician.
Downtime & Recovery: Temporary redness, dryness or peeling may occur.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid if the skin is irritated or compromised. Eye protection and precise application are essential. Dark circles caused by hollowness or visible vessels may not respond to a peel.
FAQs:
Q: Is Under-eye Peel suitable for everyone?
A: No. Suitability depends on the diagnosis, skin type, active skin conditions and the depth of peel required. A dermatologist should select the formulation and strength.

Short Description: Laser treatment often used with a carbon mask for oily skin, congestion and superficial skin refresh.
Full Description: Carbon laser treatment generally refers to laser treatment performed after application of a carbon suspension. It is often used for cosmetic skin refresh rather than deep resurfacing.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Oily skin
2. Visible pores
3. Dullness
4. Mild congestion
Key Benefits:
• May temporarily improve oiliness and skin smoothness
• Can improve visible brightness
• Usually short recovery
What To Expect: Carbon is applied to the skin and laser energy is delivered over the area using protective eyewear.
Sessions & Frequency: Often a series of treatments several weeks apart if needed.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually minimal redness or warmth.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Laser settings must be individualized; sun protection is important and darker skin has greater risk of pigmentary complications.
FAQs:
Q: Is carbon laser the same as carbon peel?
A: The terms are often used interchangeably, but protocols and devices vary. Ask the clinic which laser and protocol will be used.

Short Description: Short-pulsed Nd:YAG laser used for selected pigmentation and other pigment-containing targets.
Full Description: Q-switched Nd:YAG lasers deliver very short, high-peak-power pulses that can target pigment. The wavelength and settings are chosen according to the target and skin type.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected lentigines and superficial pigment
2. Some tattoos
3. Selected melasma/pigment protocols
4. Certain vascular/pigment targets depending on wavelength
Key Benefits:
• Precise targeting of selected pigment
• Multiple wavelengths can address different targets
• Can be used with relatively limited downtime in selected protocols
What To Expect: Protective eyewear is used. Laser pulses may feel like snapping or heat; pigment can darken, crust or fade depending on the treatment.
Sessions & Frequency: Often multiple sessions are required, with spacing based on the target and healing.
Downtime & Recovery: Mild redness and temporary darkening or crusting can occur.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Incorrect settings can cause burns or pigmentary changes. Diagnosis and experienced laser treatment are especially important in darker skin.
FAQs:
Q: Can Q-switched laser worsen pigmentation?
A: Yes, pigmentary change is a possible complication, particularly with inappropriate settings or susceptible skin, so careful assessment and sun protection matter.

Short Description: Laser-based treatment selected for specific causes and depths of unwanted pigmentation.
Full Description: There is no single 'pigmentation laser.' Clinicians select laser or light technology based on the type of pigment, depth, skin type and risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected sun spots or lentigines
2. Some post-inflammatory pigmentation
3. Selected melasma protocols
4. Other diagnosed pigment disorders
Key Benefits:
• Can target selected pigment more directly than topical care alone
• May improve uneven tone
• Treatment can be tailored to pigment type
What To Expect: The clinician first identifies the pigment source and depth, then chooses wavelength and settings. Several sessions may be needed.
Sessions & Frequency: Varies by device and diagnosis; many protocols require more than one session.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from minimal redness to several days of crusting or peeling depending on laser.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Darker skin is more susceptible to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after some lasers. Recent tanning and active inflammation increase risk.
FAQs:
Q: Will a laser permanently remove pigmentation?
A: Not necessarily. Some pigment can recur because the underlying trigger remains, and melasma in particular is chronic and relapsing.

Short Description: Laser resurfacing or scar-targeting laser treatment used to reduce the appearance of acne scars.
Full Description: Laser treatment can remodel scarred skin and stimulate collagen. The appropriate laser depends on scar type, skin tone and the balance between desired improvement and downtime.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Atrophic acne scars
2. Uneven scar texture
3. Scar-related redness or discoloration with selected lasers
4. Mixed acne-scar patterns
Key Benefits:
• Can soften scar edges and improve texture
• Stimulates collagen remodeling
• Can be combined with other scar treatments
What To Expect: The skin is prepared and laser energy is delivered in a grid or targeted pattern. Ablative treatments create more visible injury and require more recovery than non-ablative options.
Sessions & Frequency: Often multiple sessions spaced weeks to months apart depending on laser depth.
Downtime & Recovery: Non-ablative treatment may cause days of redness; ablative fractional resurfacing can require longer healing and crusting.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Active acne should usually be controlled first. Darker skin requires careful laser selection and settings because pigment changes are more likely.
FAQs:
Q: Is laser enough for every acne scar?
A: No. Rolling, boxcar and ice-pick scars respond differently, and subcision, TCA CROSS, microneedling or other treatments may be combined.

Short Description: Clinician-selected procedures used as part of acne treatment when medicines and skincare alone are insufficient.
Full Description: Acne is a medical condition with multiple causes. Procedures can sometimes complement standard acne treatment, but they are selected according to acne type, severity, scarring risk and skin sensitivity rather than used as a one-size-fits-all package.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Comedonal acne
2. Selected inflammatory acne
3. Acne-related congestion
4. Acne with early scarring risk
Key Benefits:
• Can address specific lesions or congestion
• May complement topical or oral treatment
• Treatment can be tailored to acne severity
What To Expect: The dermatologist examines the acne and may combine procedures with medical treatment. Procedure choice depends on lesion type and current inflammation.
Sessions & Frequency: Frequency varies widely; some procedures are occasional while others are performed as a short series.
Downtime & Recovery: Varies from none to several days depending on procedure.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Do not substitute cosmetic procedures for diagnosis and medical acne management. Some procedures should be avoided during active irritation or infection.
FAQs:
Q: Can procedures cure acne permanently?
A: Procedures may help control selected aspects of acne, but acne often requires an ongoing medical and skincare plan.

Short Description: Manual removal of selected blackheads and whiteheads by a trained clinician.
Full Description: Comedone extraction uses sterile instruments and controlled pressure to remove accessible comedones. It can provide immediate clearance of selected lesions but does not treat the underlying tendency to develop acne.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Blackheads
2. Whiteheads
3. Localized comedonal congestion
Key Benefits:
• Immediate removal of selected comedones
• Can reduce visible congestion
• May complement acne treatment
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed and selected comedones are gently opened and expressed. Improper pressure can injure skin, so professional technique matters.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually performed as needed rather than on a fixed course.
Downtime & Recovery: Minimal; small areas may be red or tender for a day or two.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid aggressive squeezing at home. Inflamed acne lesions are generally not appropriate for routine extraction.
FAQs:
Q: Does comedone extraction cure acne?
A: No. It removes existing comedones but does not prevent new lesions; ongoing acne management may still be needed.

Short Description: Superficial chemical peels used as an adjunct for selected acne and post-acne marks.
Full Description: Acne peels commonly use salicylic acid, glycolic acid or combination formulations to exfoliate the skin and reduce follicular congestion. They are adjunctive treatments rather than replacements for medical acne therapy.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Comedonal acne
2. Oily skin
3. Post-acne discoloration
4. Rough texture
Key Benefits:
• Helps exfoliate follicles and surface skin
• Can reduce comedonal congestion
• May improve post-acne marks
What To Expect: The peel is applied to prepared skin for a controlled period. Mild stinging, redness and later peeling may occur.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series of treatments several weeks apart when indicated.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually mild redness, dryness or peeling for a few days.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Active dermatitis, infection or significant irritation may require postponement. Sun protection is important.
FAQs:
Q: Can a chemical peel replace acne medication?
A: Usually not. Peels can complement medical acne treatment, but the underlying acne pattern determines the overall plan.

Short Description: Personalized treatment plan combining procedures according to acne-scar type and severity.
Full Description: Acne scars are not one condition. Depressed rolling, boxcar and ice-pick scars often need different approaches, and a dermatologist may combine subcision, microneedling, radiofrequency, laser, TCA CROSS or fillers.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Rolling scars
2. Boxcar scars
3. Ice-pick scars
4. Mixed acne-scar patterns
Key Benefits:
• Can make scars less noticeable
• Treatment is individualized by scar type
• Combination therapy can address different scar mechanisms
What To Expect: The dermatologist maps scar type and depth, then selects one or more procedures. Several treatment cycles are commonly needed because collagen remodeling takes time.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a multi-session plan; intervals vary by procedure and healing.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from 1–2 days for some procedures to a week or longer for more aggressive resurfacing.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Active acne should generally be controlled first. Pigment risk and healing time vary with skin type and treatment depth.
FAQs:
Q: Can acne scars be completely removed?
A: Usually the goal is improvement rather than complete removal. Different scar types respond differently and several sessions may be needed.

Short Description: Collagen-induction procedure using fine needles to create controlled micro-injuries in the skin.
Full Description: Microneedling creates numerous controlled microchannels that trigger a wound-healing response and collagen production. It is used for acne scars, texture, pores and some pigmentation concerns.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Acne scars
2. Uneven texture
3. Enlarged pores
4. Fine lines
Key Benefits:
• Stimulates collagen remodeling
• Can improve texture and scar appearance
• Generally suitable for a wide range of skin tones when properly performed
What To Expect: After topical numbing when needed, a sterile device is moved over the skin at controlled depth. Pinpoint bleeding may occur at deeper settings.
Sessions & Frequency: Often 3–6 treatments spaced about 4–6 weeks apart, but protocol varies.
Downtime & Recovery: Redness and sensitivity commonly last 1–3 days; deeper treatment can take longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid active infection, significant inflammatory skin disease and poor wound healing. Do not use non-sterile home devices for medical treatment.
FAQs:
Q: Does microneedling hurt?
A: Topical numbing can substantially reduce discomfort; patients usually feel pressure, vibration or mild prickling.

Short Description: Microneedling combined with radiofrequency energy to stimulate collagen at controlled depths.
Full Description: RF microneedling uses needles to deliver radiofrequency heat into the skin. Combining mechanical micro-injury with controlled thermal energy can stimulate collagen remodeling and is used for scars, texture and selected laxity concerns.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Acne scars
2. Skin texture
3. Enlarged pores
4. Mild skin laxity
Key Benefits:
• Combines microneedling with controlled thermal energy
• Can improve scars and texture
• Usually less surface injury than fully ablative resurfacing
What To Expect: Topical numbing is commonly used. Needles enter the skin and radiofrequency energy is delivered at selected depths before the device is withdrawn.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series of about 3–4 treatments spaced several weeks apart, depending on device and indication.
Downtime & Recovery: Redness, swelling and pinpoint marks commonly last a few days.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Device settings and needle depth matter. Burns and pigment changes are possible, particularly with poor technique. Avoid active infection or significant inflammation.
FAQs:
Q: Is RF microneedling the same as regular microneedling?
A: No. RF microneedling adds radiofrequency heat below the skin surface, so the treatment depth and energy settings differ.

Short Description: Minor procedure that releases fibrous bands tethering depressed acne scars to deeper tissue.
Full Description: Subcision uses a needle or cannula placed beneath a depressed scar to sever fibrous attachments that pull the scar downward. It is particularly relevant to rolling or tethered scars.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Rolling acne scars
2. Tethered depressed scars
3. Selected depressed traumatic scars
Key Benefits:
• Releases tethered scar tissue
• Can raise depressed scars
• Often combined with resurfacing or fillers for mixed scar patterns
What To Expect: After local anesthesia, a needle or cannula is passed beneath the scar to release fibrous bands. Bruising and swelling are common afterward.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a series separated by several weeks to months depending on scar response.
Downtime & Recovery: Bruising, swelling and tenderness can last several days; occasionally longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Infection, hematoma, post-inflammatory pigment change and irregular contour are possible. Procedure should be performed by an experienced clinician.
FAQs:
Q: Does subcision work for ice-pick scars?
A: It is generally more useful for rolling/tethered scars. Ice-pick scars often need a focal treatment such as TCA CROSS or another approach.

Short Description: Focal trichloroacetic-acid application used mainly for ice-pick and selected boxcar acne scars.
Full Description: TCA CROSS means chemical reconstruction of skin scars. High-concentration TCA is applied precisely inside selected atrophic scars to stimulate localized remodeling. It is not the same as applying a TCA peel to the whole face.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Ice-pick acne scars
2. Deep narrow boxcar scars
3. Selected atrophic scars
Key Benefits:
• Targets individual depressed scars
• Can improve scar depth over multiple treatments
• Can complement resurfacing or subcision
What To Expect: The clinician applies TCA focally into individual scar depressions. A white frosting reaction is expected at the treated sites, followed by crusting and healing.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually multiple sessions separated by several weeks; exact frequency depends on response and skin type.
Downtime & Recovery: Crusting and redness can last several days; pigment changes may persist longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Higher concentrations increase risk of post-inflammatory pigment changes and scarring if misapplied. Precise professional application is essential, especially in darker skin.
FAQs:
Q: Is TCA CROSS the same as a TCA facial peel?
A: No. CROSS applies TCA focally inside individual scars, whereas a peel treats a broader skin area.

Short Description: Diagnosis-led treatment for excess skin pigment using sun protection, topical therapy and selected procedures.
Full Description: Hyperpigmentation has many causes, including melasma, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and sun-induced pigment. Treatment should begin by identifying the cause; procedures may include chemical peels, lasers or light treatments in selected patients.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Melasma
2. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
3. Sun spots
4. Uneven facial tone
Key Benefits:
• Targets the cause and appearance of excess pigment
• Can combine home treatment with procedures
• Long-term control is possible for some conditions, although recurrence can occur
What To Expect: The clinician evaluates distribution, triggers and skin type. Treatment may combine daily photoprotection with topical agents and, when appropriate, a procedure.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a longer-term plan; procedural sessions vary by diagnosis and response.
Downtime & Recovery: Depends on the treatment selected, from none to several days.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Sun protection is central. Aggressive procedures can worsen pigmentation, especially in darker skin. Melasma often needs ongoing maintenance.
FAQs:
Q: Can hyperpigmentation be permanently cured?
A: It depends on the cause. Some spots can be treated effectively, while conditions such as melasma commonly recur without maintenance and trigger control.

Short Description: Umbrella category covering non-surgical treatments for wrinkles, volume loss, pigmentation and skin laxity.
Full Description: Anti-ageing treatment is a category, not a single procedure. Depending on the concern, clinicians may use botulinum toxin, fillers, lasers, peels, microneedling, radiofrequency, ultrasound or skin-quality treatments.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Fine lines and wrinkles
2. Loss of facial volume
3. Skin laxity
4. Photoaging and uneven texture
Key Benefits:
• Addresses different components of facial ageing
• Can be tailored to specific concerns
• Non-surgical options can provide gradual or targeted changes
What To Expect: A clinician assesses facial movement, skin quality, volume and laxity before recommending treatments. Different procedures have very different risks and recovery.
Sessions & Frequency: Varies from one-time treatments to maintenance every few months or years depending on modality.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from none to several days or longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Realistic expectations are important. Injectable and energy-based procedures carry procedure-specific risks and should be performed by appropriately trained clinicians.
FAQs:
Q: What is the best anti-ageing procedure?
A: It depends on whether the main issue is movement-related lines, volume loss, skin quality or laxity.

Short Description: Injectable botulinum toxin that temporarily reduces targeted muscle activity to soften dynamic lines.
Full Description: Botulinum toxin is a prescription medicine injected into selected muscles. It reduces nerve-to-muscle signaling, temporarily weakening the targeted muscle and softening dynamic wrinkles. It is also used medically for conditions such as excessive sweating.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Frown lines
2. Forehead lines
3. Crow's feet
4. Selected facial muscle-related concerns
Key Benefits:
• Softens dynamic facial lines
• Results develop over several days
• Treatment is quick and does not require surgery
What To Expect: A clinician maps facial movement and injects small amounts into selected muscles. Small bumps, redness or bruising can occur temporarily.
Sessions & Frequency: Effects commonly become noticeable within days and last about 3–4 months, though duration varies by person and area.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually no meaningful downtime; small injection-site bumps or bruises can occur.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Must be prescribed and administered in an appropriate medical setting. Tell the clinician about neuromuscular disorders, pregnancy/breastfeeding and medications.
FAQs:
Q: Will Botox freeze my face?
A: Appropriate dosing aims to reduce targeted muscle activity while preserving natural expression; excessive or misplaced treatment can produce unwanted weakness.

Short Description: Injectable materials used to restore volume, soften selected lines and enhance facial contours.
Full Description: Dermal fillers are injectable medical devices/materials. Hyaluronic acid is commonly used, while other filler materials have different properties and durations. Fillers can add volume to lips, cheeks, chin or other areas and may also improve selected scars.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Facial volume loss
2. Lip augmentation
3. Cheek or chin contouring
4. Selected folds and scars
Key Benefits:
• Immediate volume change with many fillers
• Can restore or reshape selected facial areas
• Some hyaluronic-acid fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase when clinically appropriate
What To Expect: The clinician assesses anatomy and goals, cleans the skin and injects filler using a needle or cannula. Swelling and bruising are common after treatment.
Sessions & Frequency: Often one treatment with review after swelling settles; duration depends strongly on product, area and metabolism.
Downtime & Recovery: Swelling, tenderness and bruising commonly last several days; some areas can remain swollen longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Rare but serious vascular complications can occur. Fillers should only be injected by an appropriately trained medical professional using approved products.
FAQs:
Q: Are all fillers reversible?
A: No. Hyaluronic-acid fillers can often be treated with hyaluronidase, but other filler materials may not be readily reversible.

Short Description: Injectable skin-quality treatment intended to improve hydration and selected aspects of skin texture and elasticity.
Full Description: Skin boosters are a broad category of injectable products placed superficially or within the dermis. Formulations vary and may include hyaluronic acid or other materials, so evidence, indications and duration depend on the specific product.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Dehydrated-looking skin
2. Fine superficial lines
3. Reduced skin elasticity
4. Skin-quality concerns
Key Benefits:
• Can improve hydration and skin quality
• Usually changes skin quality rather than facial structure
• Some products may stimulate collagen or other remodeling responses
What To Expect: The clinician cleans the skin, may apply numbing, and delivers multiple small injections across the treatment area.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as an initial series followed by maintenance; exact schedule is product-specific.
Downtime & Recovery: Small bumps, redness, swelling or bruising can occur for a few days.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • The term 'skin booster' covers different products. Patients should ask exactly what product is being injected, its approved use and potential complications.
FAQs:
Q: Are skin boosters the same as dermal fillers?
A: Not exactly. Skin boosters are generally intended to improve skin quality and hydration, while fillers are primarily used to add or restore volume, although products can overlap.

Short Description: Autologous platelet-rich plasma used on facial skin, often alongside microneedling or injections.
Full Description: PRP facial treatment uses a patient's own blood, processed to concentrate platelets and growth factors. PRP may be applied during microneedling or injected, with evidence varying by indication and protocol.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Skin texture
2. Fine lines
3. Acne scars as an adjunct
4. Selected skin-quality concerns
Key Benefits:
• Uses the patient's own blood product
• May support collagen remodeling
• Can be combined with microneedling in some protocols
What To Expect: A small blood sample is drawn and centrifuged. The platelet-rich portion is then applied or injected according to the selected protocol.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed as a series of treatments spaced several weeks apart; exact protocol varies.
Downtime & Recovery: Redness, swelling, pinpoint bleeding or bruising can occur, particularly when combined with microneedling or injections.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Evidence varies by indication. Sterile processing is essential. Tell the clinician about bleeding disorders and medications that affect clotting.
FAQs:
Q: Is PRP a permanent skin treatment?
A: No. Any improvement is not necessarily permanent, and the strength of evidence varies by indication and treatment protocol.

Short Description: Non-surgical radiofrequency treatment that heats deeper skin layers to stimulate collagen remodeling and improve firmness.
Full Description: Radiofrequency devices deliver electromagnetic energy that produces controlled heating in tissue. Over time, the wound-healing response can increase collagen remodeling and improve the appearance of mild skin laxity.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Mild facial skin laxity
2. Neck laxity
3. Fine lines
4. Selected body skin laxity
Key Benefits:
• Non-surgical approach to mild laxity
• Can improve firmness and texture gradually
• Usually little interruption to daily activities
What To Expect: The skin is cleansed and a handpiece is moved over the treatment area. Patients typically feel warmth and sometimes tingling.
Sessions & Frequency: Some people need 2–6 treatments; others may receive a single treatment depending on device and goals. Changes can develop over months.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually minimal; temporary redness or swelling may occur.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Excessive energy can cause burns. Device choice and settings matter, and active skin disease should be discussed with the clinician.
FAQs:
Q: How quickly does RF tightening work?
A: Some changes can be noticed early, but collagen remodeling develops over months and results vary by device and patient.

Short Description: Focused ultrasound treatment used to create controlled thermal effects at selected depths for skin tightening.
Full Description: HIFU uses focused ultrasound energy to create small zones of heating at targeted depths. It is a non-surgical option for selected mild-to-moderate laxity, but outcomes depend on device, treatment depth and patient anatomy.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Mild to moderate facial laxity
2. Jawline definition
3. Neck laxity
4. Selected brow/cheek lifting goals
Key Benefits:
• Non-surgical tightening approach
• Targets deeper tissue without an incision
• Results develop gradually as tissue remodels
What To Expect: Ultrasound gel is applied and the handpiece delivers focused pulses at selected depths. Patients may feel heat, tingling or brief discomfort.
Sessions & Frequency: Some protocols use one treatment with reassessment; others may use repeat treatment depending on response.
Downtime & Recovery: Usually little downtime; tenderness or swelling can occur temporarily.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Appropriate depth and energy settings are important. Results are generally more modest than surgery and vary with skin laxity and anatomy.
FAQs:
Q: Is HIFU a replacement for a facelift?
A: No. HIFU is non-surgical and generally provides more subtle tightening than surgical lifting.

Short Description: Minimally invasive lifting procedure using absorbable medical threads placed under the skin.
Full Description: Thread lift procedures place medical-grade threads under the skin to provide a mechanical lifting effect and stimulate a local healing response. Results are generally subtle and temporary compared with surgical lifting.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Early facial laxity
2. Selected jawline or cheek laxity
3. Selected neck laxity
4. Mild brow lifting in appropriate cases
Key Benefits:
• Can provide a subtle lifting effect
• Minimally invasive compared with a facelift
• Usually short recovery
What To Expect: Local anesthesia is used. Threads are inserted with a needle or cannula and positioned under the skin. Swelling, bruising and soreness are common.
Sessions & Frequency: Results are temporary; many sources report roughly 1–3 years depending on thread and patient, with gradual loss as threads are absorbed.
Downtime & Recovery: Bruising and swelling can last several days; tenderness may persist longer.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Potential complications include infection, bleeding, asymmetry, dimpling or thread visibility/palpability. Appropriate patient selection is important.
FAQs:
Q: Is a thread lift permanent?
A: No. The threads are generally absorbable and the lifting effect is temporary.

Short Description: Treatment planning to change or restore facial proportions using injectables, devices or other procedures.
Full Description: Facial contouring is a treatment goal rather than one procedure. Depending on anatomy and the desired change, a clinician may use fillers, botulinum toxin, energy-based treatment or, in selected cases, surgery.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Cheek definition
2. Chin projection
3. Jawline definition
4. Selected jowl or facial-volume concerns
Key Benefits:
• Can alter facial proportions without surgery in selected cases
• Treatment can be individualized to anatomy
• Different modalities address volume, muscle or laxity
What To Expect: A clinician assesses facial symmetry, bone structure, soft tissue volume and skin laxity before selecting an approach.
Sessions & Frequency: Depends on modality; fillers may be one session with review, while energy treatments may require a series.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from none to several days of swelling/bruising depending on procedure.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Facial anatomy and vascular risk matter, especially with fillers. Results and suitability should be discussed using realistic expectations.
FAQs:
Q: Does facial contouring always mean fillers?
A: No. Contouring can involve fillers, muscle-relaxing injections, energy treatments or surgery depending on the specific anatomical goal.

Short Description: Autologous platelet-rich plasma injections used as an adjunct treatment for selected types of hair loss.
Full Description: PRP therapy for hair loss uses a patient's own blood, processed to concentrate platelets, then injected into areas of thinning. Evidence supports possible benefit for some patients, particularly androgenetic alopecia, but response is variable and PRP does not replace diagnosis or standard treatment.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Androgenetic/pattern hair loss
2. Selected diffuse thinning
3. Selected hair-loss conditions after diagnosis
Key Benefits:
• Uses the patient's own blood product
• May improve hair density in some patients
• Can be combined with established hair-loss treatments
What To Expect: Blood is drawn and centrifuged, and the platelet-rich fraction is injected into the scalp after appropriate preparation and numbing.
Sessions & Frequency: Often an initial series of treatments followed by maintenance; exact protocol varies widely.
Downtime & Recovery: Scalp tenderness, swelling or headache can occur for a day or two; usually little downtime.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Hair loss has many causes. Diagnosis is important before PRP. Results are variable and maintenance may be needed.
FAQs:
Q: Does PRP regrow hair for everyone?
A: No. Evidence is strongest for selected hair-loss disorders and response varies between patients.

Short Description: Diagnosis-led treatment plan for hair shedding or thinning using medical therapy and selected procedures.
Full Description: Hair loss can result from androgenetic alopecia, telogen effluvium, alopecia areata, nutritional or hormonal factors and other conditions. Management begins with diagnosis and may include medicines, lifestyle correction, PRP, low-level light therapy or referral for hair transplantation when appropriate.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Pattern hair loss
2. Excessive shedding
3. Diffuse thinning
4. Selected alopecia disorders
Key Benefits:
• Identifies the underlying cause
• Can combine medical and procedural options
• Earlier diagnosis can help prevent unnecessary treatment
What To Expect: The clinician reviews onset, pattern, medical history and scalp findings. Dermoscopy and selected laboratory tests may be used before treatment is chosen.
Sessions & Frequency: There is no universal session schedule; medication and procedural plans depend on diagnosis and response.
Downtime & Recovery: Varies by treatment; procedures may cause short-term scalp tenderness.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Do not treat unexplained hair loss solely as a cosmetic issue. Pregnancy, medications and medical conditions can affect treatment choice.
FAQs:
Q: Is hair fall always treated with PRP?
A: No. PRP is only one option and may not be appropriate for the underlying cause.

Short Description: Clinician-selected treatments for scalp health, dandruff, inflammation or hair-growth concerns.
Full Description: Scalp treatment is an umbrella term. Depending on the diagnosis, management may include medicated topical therapy, procedures such as PRP or microneedling, or treatment of seborrheic dermatitis and other scalp conditions.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Scalp inflammation
2. Dandruff/seborrheic dermatitis
3. Hair thinning
4. Scalp dryness or oiliness
Key Benefits:
• Treats the underlying scalp condition
• Can support hair-loss management when appropriate
• Treatment is tailored to diagnosis
What To Expect: The scalp is examined and the cause of symptoms is identified. The plan may include medication, procedures or both.
Sessions & Frequency: Depends entirely on diagnosis and treatment; procedural courses may involve multiple visits.
Downtime & Recovery: Ranges from none to a few days of tenderness or redness after procedures.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Avoid self-treating persistent hair loss or severe scalp inflammation without diagnosis. Tell the clinician about medications and previous treatments.
FAQs:
Q: Can a scalp treatment stop hair loss by itself?
A: Only if it addresses the underlying cause; many types of hair loss require diagnosis-specific medical treatment.

Short Description: Scalp microneedling used as an adjunct for selected hair-loss conditions.
Full Description: Microneedling creates controlled micro-injuries in the scalp and may stimulate wound-healing pathways. Some studies suggest benefit when combined with standard treatments for androgenetic hair loss, but evidence and protocols vary.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Selected androgenetic alopecia
2. Hair thinning as an adjunct to medical therapy
3. Selected scalp treatment protocols
Key Benefits:
• May stimulate local healing responses
• May improve delivery of topical treatments in some protocols
• Can be combined with other hair-loss therapies
What To Expect: The scalp is cleaned and the device is passed over thinning areas at a clinician-selected depth. Mild pinpoint bleeding may occur.
Sessions & Frequency: Often performed weekly to monthly depending on protocol; evidence does not support one universal schedule.
Downtime & Recovery: Tenderness, redness and mild swelling can occur for a day or two.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Diagnosis is essential. Device depth differs from facial microneedling and improper technique can cause infection or scarring.
FAQs:
Q: Is scalp microneedling a standalone cure for hair loss?
A: No. Evidence is mainly as an adjunct for selected hair-loss disorders and it should follow diagnosis.

Short Description: Laser treatment that targets hair follicles to produce long-term reduction in unwanted body hair.
Full Description: Laser hair removal/reduction uses selected wavelengths absorbed by melanin in the hair follicle. Multiple sessions are needed because hairs respond best during particular growth phases. It is generally described as permanent hair reduction rather than guaranteed complete removal.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Legs and arms
2. Underarms
3. Back and chest
4. Bikini/body hair
Key Benefits:
• Long-term reduction in hair growth
• Can reduce shaving and ingrown-hair problems in selected patients
• Treatment is relatively quick for many body areas
What To Expect: The area is shaved as instructed and laser pulses are delivered with cooling. A snapping or warm sensation is common. Hair sheds over the following days or weeks.
Sessions & Frequency: Commonly about 6–8 sessions spaced roughly 4–8 weeks apart, followed by maintenance when needed; exact schedule varies by area and hair cycle.
Downtime & Recovery: Redness and follicular swelling are common for several hours; pigment changes or burns are uncommon but possible.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Recent tanning increases risk. Laser choice should account for skin tone and hair colour; very light, grey or white hair responds poorly because of limited melanin.
FAQs:
Q: Is laser hair removal completely permanent?
A: It is better described as long-term hair reduction. Some hairs can regrow and maintenance may be needed.

Short Description: Superficial chemical peels used on selected body areas for texture, acne, pigmentation or keratosis-related concerns.
Full Description: Body chemical peels use acids such as salicylic, glycolic, lactic or TCA depending on the diagnosis and body site. Skin thickness and pigment risk vary across body areas, so strength must be individualized.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Body acne
2. Post-inflammatory pigmentation
3. Rough texture
4. Selected keratosis or follicular congestion
Key Benefits:
• Exfoliates superficial skin
• Can improve selected pigment and texture concerns
• Can complement topical treatment
What To Expect: The area is cleansed and the chosen peel is applied for a controlled time, then removed or neutralized as required.
Sessions & Frequency: Usually a series spaced several weeks apart when indicated.
Downtime & Recovery: Dryness, redness and peeling can occur for several days.
Clinical Considerations & Precautions: • Body skin can also develop post-inflammatory pigmentation. Avoid use on irritated, infected or recently waxed/shaved skin unless advised by the clinician.
FAQs:
Q: Are body peels stronger than facial peels?
A: Not automatically. The correct strength depends on the body area, diagnosis and patient's skin response.

Short Description: Diagnosis-led treatment for dark patches or uneven pigmentation on body skin.
Full Description: Body pigmentation can follow acne, friction, inflammation, hormones or other conditions. Treatment may combine trigger control, topical therapy and selected peels or lasers after the cause is established.
Common Uses / Indications:
1. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation
2. Friction-related darkening
3. Selected sun-related pigmentation
4. Uneven body tone
Key Benefits:
• Addresses the cause as well as visible pigment
• Can improve uneven tone gradually
• Treatment can be tailored to body site and skin type
